When 3 of the biggest Android OEMs use notification trays to deliver ads, it's hard not to look at iOS and wonder if it's a more consumer-friendly platform.
When apple has exclusive control over what I can add or remove from my device, it's hard to believe that it is a consumer friendly platform.
I think personally it depends at what angle you look at "consumer friendliness", however I do think that that is one of iOS's best features while simultaneously being its biggest limitation.

The entire Google Play store is designed to deliver and dish out ads just about. When I first got my device and still used Google stuff I gave up on the store very quickly. Coming from Symbian where there was tonnes of free stuff that was 99% awesome and useful and 100% ad free it was really hard to swallow the rubbish that Android seemed to be offering me. Although there are a few gems if you dig deep enough through all the poop, you're going to be digging for a long time and you're going to pick up more petrified poop then rubies. From my experience of Android since the start (before ditching the stock firmware and Google) this seems perfectly fitting and perfectly in character for that little green advert machine.

That said, I'd still get another Android device rather then an 'i' device.
Thats why I run Cyanogenmod on my OnePlus. no bloatware and I dont even have to install the google apps if I dont want them.

if you use a nexus you will never have to worry about ads getting onto your android and you will honestly have the best android experience.

i think of the nexus line as the iphone of the androids

Some would say I have "too" many knives. But I use most of them regularly. I do tend to settle into routines though.

Right now. Kershaw Skyline for work, holds an edge and takes a beating at the warehouse. Weekends/time away from work is my Esee Izula 2.

Whats your situation?
Do you have just one knife, or a rotation of them?

if you carry a knife everyday one is never enough. different knifes for different purposes. gotta have a small fixed blade for hiking a large fixed blade for camp. small or medium folder for every day carry. stainless blade for fishing or swimming. plus a nice looking knife for special occasions. gotta have some nice knifes in the kitchen, and a couple beaters. maybe you buy a couple you end up not loving so they sit in a drawer. when my wife says i have too many knifes i just ask her about shoes.

My go to is always make up. She doesn't really have a shoe problem.

Now that you mention it I don't really have a fancy, or dress type knife. What's your dress knife?
opinal no 9 with my initials on the blade, I sanded the handle to a superfine finish and stained it a red oak color.
I have never had the chance to handle an opinel. They look uncomfortable to me, but looks can be deceiving.

It fits the hand nicely. Slices like a dream with the thin blade. You will hold it slightly different than your standard folder. If i were you i would pick one up their less than 20 for a basic. They look very nice and are great when you want something very non tactical looking. Also the lock collar ring makes them very stable feeling.
Opinal knives are awesome. Get one. Then another. And then a couple more.

I've got a Buck folder I picked up in Nevada. It's one of the smaller ones and is a double blade folder, one smaller blade and one larger blade. I like to use the smaller blade as my beater and keep the larger blade sharp and ready if something needs to be cut fast. That's my usual daily carry for work or going outdoors. If I dress up (k)nice I carry a Utica Cutlery folder with a horn handle. It's got a real nice shine and look to it that people don't freak out if I need to use it. The one thing I've noticed is that people generally think folders with wood, bone and other natural handles look more "classy" or sophisticated/old-timey and are less likely to throw a hissy fit over you carrying. But any of the synthetic or tactical-type folders, people think you're some kind of psycho. shrug Not like it really matters though.
